BiblicalUsage: Adoni-bezek was the Canaanite king of Bezek, defeated by Judah and Simeon at the start of the conquest. They cut off his thumbs and great toes, and he confessed that he had done the same to seventy kings — and that God had repaid him as he had done.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Adoni-bezek's confession is the point of his story: 'As I have done, so God hath requited me.' It is the law of sowing and reaping, spoken by a defeated king, and it stands as a warning that cruelty comes home.
